title: Echo Pairs
statement:
You are given an array `a[1], a[2], ..., a[n]` and an integer `k`.

A pair of positions `(i, j)` with `i < j` is an *echo pair* if `a[i] = a[j]` and `j - i ≥ k`. Each pair of positions is counted once.

Count the echo pairs.
inputFormat:
Line 1: two integers `n` and `k`, separated by a single space.
Line 2: `n` integers `a[1] ... a[n]`, separated by single spaces.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the number of echo pairs. If there are none, print `0`.

samples.explanation: Value 3 is at positions 1, 3, 4, 7. Its pairs with distance at least 3 are (1,4), (1,7), (3,7), (4,7); the pairs (1,3) and (3,4) are too close. Value 1 is at positions 2 and 6, distance 4, so (2,6) counts. Value 2 appears once. Answer: 4 + 1 = 5.
All values are equal and every distance is at least 1, so all 6 pairs of positions count: (1,2), (1,3), (1,4), (2,3), (2,4), (3,4). Answer: 6.
No value appears twice, so there are no echo pairs. Answer: 0.
